summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, and multiple prior surgeries was admitted for fever, rigors, and worsening left lower quadrant abdominal pain with distention and vomiting. Imaging showed no mechanical obstruction but revealed a fixed stricture at the ileocolonic anastomosis and new areas of bowel wall thickening likely due to peristalsis. She was treated for a presumed Crohn’s flare with antibiotics (ciprofloxacin, metronidazole, and later rifaximin), bowel rest, and NG tube decompression. A colonoscopy confirmed active inflammation and stricture, which was dilated. IV iron was given for iron deficiency anemia, and her acute kidney injury resolved with hydration. Her PTSD and anxiety were managed with diazepam, which was transitioned to oral taper. She gradually improved, tolerated a full diet, and was discharged home on oral medications with follow-up plans.
